PK/PD models rarely simulate DNA. They simulate **exposure** and a **phenotype** — often an MIC or a kill curve. Genetics still matters, because it tells you how stable that phenotype is and how it might spread between patients or species.

This secondary-track lesson is a bridge: enough bacterial genetics to stop treating every MIC as the same kind of object.

::: {.callout-note}
## Scope
Genetics-for-modelers, not a full genomics course. Pair with the PK/PD track starting at [targets and MIC](01-pkpd-targets-and-mic.qmd).
:::

## Two genomic homes for resistance

| Feature | Chromosomal | Plasmid-borne (typical) |
|---------|-------------|-------------------------|
| Inheritance | Vertical (mother → daughter) | Vertical **and** often horizontal |
| Dose effect | Usually one/few copies per genome | Copy number can amplify expression |
| Mobility | Mostly within lineage | Can jump lineages / species |
| Modeling implication | Phenotype more lineage-stable | MIC ecology can shift faster; local epidemiology ages quicker |

A chromosomal target-site mutation and a plasmid β-lactamase can produce the “same” higher MIC in a table — and very different public-health and uncertainty stories.

## What changes inside a PK/PD workflow

1. **MIC distribution provenance**  
   If resistance is plasmid-driven and locally epidemic, last year’s surveillance weights may be stale.

2. **Heterogeneity inside “one MIC”**  
   Same categorical MIC breakpoint can hide different enzyme burdens or copy numbers.

3. **Combination regimens**  
   Inhibitor partners (for example avibactam) are meaningful when the mechanism is enzyme-mediated; they are the wrong lever for some chromosomal target mutations.

4. **Uncertainty labeling**  
   Mark whether MIC inputs reflect a stable clonal background or a mobile element–shaped ecology.

## Takeaway for modelers

- Do not ask genetics to replace PK/PD; ask it to **annotate the MIC layer**.
- Plasmid ecology → refresh surveillance weights and mechanism assumptions more aggressively.
- Chromosomal lineage structure → stability helps, but still verify assay and species ID.
